title: Percentile-Watch orchestration playbook: per-route/model/region p95 & p99 telemetry
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We need a reproducible, low-noise way to detect regressions in tail latency (p95/p99) with routing resolution down to route + model + region. Current signals are noisy across bursty traffic patterns and lack clear attribution to model variant or region. Goal: define an orchestration playbook that ties synthetic loadbench runs to live telemetry, produces per-slice p95/p99 dashboards, and establishes automated regression gates and alerting playbooks. Deliverables: (1) a sampling and loadbench topology that exercises tokens/sec distributions representative of production routes, (2) ingestion schema and rollups for p50/p90/p95/p99 per (route, model, region, lane), (3) Grafana dashboard templates and a lightweight indexer for slice diffs, (4) regression detection rules that combine statistical tests (CDF shift + bootstrap confidence) with production volume weighting, (5) an incident playbook describing fallback routing, canary rollback, and notes for SE/PM triage.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic loadbench profiles defined and checked in; each route has at least one synthesized traffic signature covering long-tail token distributions
Time-series ingestion emits p50/p90/p95/p99 per 1m for every (route, model, region) and stores 90 days of high-res samples
Grafana dashboard template with per-slice comparator and heatmap is available; dashboards accept route/model/region variables
Regression watcher runs nightly and raises a P1 pager only when statistical threshold + volume condition are met; reproducer loadbench link included in alert
Playbook documents rollback steps (route-level fallback, model-variant fallback, capacity scaling) and ownership handoff for on-call
notes_and_decisions: We will prefer 1-minute rollups for percentile computation with a separate high-cardinality archive for forensic playback (sampled traces). This balances alert latency with cost.
Percentile computation approach: use t-digest for streaming aggregation for p50/p90/p95 and a bootstrap-on-window for p99 to reduce sensitivity to single outliers.
Loadbench topology: combine 'steady-state' token/sec profiles + 'spike' sequences. Each synthetic profile is parameterized by mean tokens/sec, variance, model context length, and prompt temperature.

Regression detection: require (a) >= 2x increase in p99 vs baseline OR absolute delta > 50ms AND (b) traffic volume in the slice above minimum threshold (1000 requests in last hour) to fire a high-severity alert.
We intentionally avoid relying solely on z-score-style detectors because heavy-tailed latency distributions violate normal assumptions; instead use non-parametric CDF distance + bootstrap p-value.

Retention trade-off: high-res per-request traces kept for 7 days; aggregated percentile archive kept 90 days. Forensic playback uses sampled tokens with hashed prompt fingerprints to reconstruct representative workloads.
Security: dashboards contain no customer prompt content; sampled reproducer payloads are hashed and redacted by default. KMS usage handled by infra team (see dependency list).
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: spike/steady synthetic profiles sketched. Initial list of 18 routes selected covering 80% of tokens/sec volume (PR: github.com/redwood/inferbench/pulls/312).
2025-02-18: aggregator proto baked in telemetry agent; t-digest library evaluated (chosen implementation: tdigest-go). Prototype produces p95 within 2% of offline baseline.
2025-02-24: Grafana panels prototype created (dashboard: grafana.redwood.company/d/dq3Yj8/percentile-watch). Shared with PM and Design for feedback.
2025-03-01: regression watcher prototype completed. Initial rule set generates too many false-positives on low-volume slices; added volume gating and bootstrap filter.

2025-03-04: engineering review completed. Plan to iterate on alert suppression heuristics and add a 'replay-to-pipeline' link in alerts to kick off deterministic playback runs. Assigned follow-up tasks for infra to provision retention bucket.
review_feedback: PM (Avery Brooks): prefer prioritizing top-10 revenue routes for initial rollout and include a summary card in Console's route overview.
SRE (Riley Thompson): asked to add graceful alert suppression for maintenance windows and to integrate with on-call runbook links.
Design (Samira Ortiz): requested heatmap color accessibility tweaks and suggested adding a small 'explainability' panel showing token/sec distribution and sample prompts (redacted).
Security (Jordan Li): confirmed hashed reproducer payloads meet compliance surface but requested an explicit opt-out for storing any customer-derived fingerprints.
customer_notes: PM wants this in the console as an optional card for enterprise tenants. Will coordinate with sales for early trials.
operational_playbook: Contains steps: (1) when alert fires, run repro link -> schedule 1-hour reserved-run on Dedicated pool, (2) if repro confirms latency regression, scale up model variant or route fallback for 30 minutes, (3) open incident with model-owner tag and attach percentiles diff and loadbench artifact.
implementation_tips: - Use tdigest for live percentiles; keep a rolling buffer for bootstrap samples.

Add volume-gated heuristic to watcher and test against two weeks of historical traces
Roll out dashboard to internal teams, collect feedback, then enable for top-10 revenue routes
